translations.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to the Gentiles who are loved by God the Father, kept by Jesus Christ, and chosen.
May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

Beloved, although I was making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I felt compelled to write to you and urge you to contend for the faith that was entrusted to the saints once for all.

For certain people have slipped in, ungodly people who were long ago destined for this judgment. They have turned the grace of our God into lawlessness and denied the only Master and our Lord Jesus Christ.
I now wish to remind you, who know all things, that God once saved the people from Egypt, but afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
And the angels who did not keep their own authority but abandoned their dwelling, he has kept in darkness with everlasting chains for the judgment of the great day.

Likewise, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, which committed sexual immorality in the same way and pursued the flesh of others, stand as an example, having received the judgment of eternal fire.
In the same way, these people also, as though delirious in sleep, defile the flesh, despise authorities, and blaspheme the glorious ones.

Yet Michael the archangel, when he disputed with the devil Satan and answered him concerning the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a blasphemous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”
But these people blaspheme whatever they do not understand; and even in the things they know by instinct, like speechless animals, they will be corrupted.
Woe to them, for they have followed the way of Cain, abandoned themselves to Balaam’s error in pursuit of payment, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.

These are hated complainers who follow their own desires. At their love feasts they deceitfully join you in celebration, feeding themselves without fear. They are waterless clouds driven by the wind, trees that have lost their fruit, fruitless, twice dead, uprooted.
They are uncontrollable waves of the sea, constantly foaming up their own shame, wandering stars for whom the abyss of darkness has been reserved forever.
Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them, saying, “Look, the Lord came with tens of thousands of holy angels
to carry out judgment in all things and to convict all the ungodly concerning the deeds they committed in ungodliness and concerning all the harsh words that ungodly sinners spoke against him.”
These are grumblers and complainers, following their own desires. Their mouths speak arrogant things, and they flatter people for their own advantage.
But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For they told you, “In the last times there will be scornful people who follow their own ungodly desires.”
These are the notorious ones, worldly people who do not have the Spirit.
But let us, beloved, build ourselves up in the holiness of faith; let us continue in prayer in the Holy Spirit,
keeping ourselves in the love of God and awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ for eternal life.
And rebuke some who have been condemned.
And save some by snatching them out of the fire, and show mercy to some with fear, judging even the garment that has been defiled by the flesh.
And to him who is able to keep you faultless and spotless, firmly established before his glory without fear and with joy,
To the only God and our Savior, Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, greatness, power, and authority, before all ages, both now and for all ages. Amen.
